originality.rationale: A highly relevant published SCOPE result gives the stronger family formula \(\dim_F MH^{P,Q}_{3,4}=q^2\) for ordered distinct same-side endpoints in every projective-plane incidence graph. At \(q=2\) those \(84\) localized summands already contribute \(336\). However that theorem explicitly does not compute equal-endpoint summands, so it supplies a lower bound on the total group rather than the submitted equality. The audited total computation adds the complementary statement that every equal-endpoint summand vanishes; mixed endpoints have no chains by bipartite parity. Neither the girth theorem nor the geodetic theorem gives that vanishing. Thus the exact total rank is not literally covered, although most of its positive contribution is.
residual_risks: The novelty margin is narrow because a stronger published SCOPE theorem already determines every positive distinct same-side contribution; the surviving new content is the vanishing of the complementary endpoint summands.

value.rationale: The Fano-plane incidence graph is the smallest canonical projective-plane example at the sharp girth-six boundary. Determining whether the general endpoint-localized contribution exhausts the entire first off-diagonal group is a natural completion question; the exact total rank answers it affirmatively and supplies a benchmark for separating localized from global magnitude homology.

final_claim: For the Heawood graph \(H\), presented as the Fano-plane incidence graph with its shortest-path metric, \(\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{MH}_{3,4}(H;\mathbb F_2)=336\).
